newsitem.title: UK: Vietnam plans to become sugar exporter by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam plans to become sugar exporter by 2000.

text.p: Vietnam plans to produce one million tonnes of sugar a year before the year 2000 and then become a net exporter, the deputy director general of industry producer Vinasugar II said on Wednesday.

Vietnam produced 10.71 million tonnes of cane in 1995, sharply up from the 7.55 million in the previous year, said Nguyen Van Chap in a prepared speech at a two-day seminar hosted by the International Sugar Organization (ISO).
Van Chap said Vietnam planned to expand its processing mills towards the year 2000, increasing the 16 existing plants with a daily cane processing capacity of 20,150 tonnes to 49.

This would bring the country's total cane output to 99,850 tonnes a day, he said. The ISO has forecast Vietnamese sugar production at 550,000 tonnes raw value in 1996/97, unchanged from the previous year.
It said Vietnam imported 188,039 tonnes of sugar in 1995, up from 140,688 in 1994, mainly from Thailand.
